subject: Urgent: HelioHealth throughput outage — proposed SLA settlement
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@heliohealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliohealth.com>, Eve Stanton <eve.stanton@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Severe throughput degradation impacting Q4 batch jobs

Rafael,

We experienced a major throughput regression on Tuesday evening (around 20:15 PST) that caused several of our end-of-quarter inference batches to fail. Error rates spiked to ~18% and median latency jumped from 120ms to 1.2s. That resulted in missed SLAs to our downstream analytics partners and a manual rerun this morning.

This is a high-severity customer-impact event for HelioHealth. We need an explanation, concrete remediation, and to discuss commercial remediation (credits or other). Can we get a timeline and an exec-level contact for this?

Alex
Director of Engineering
HelioHealth

(Attachment: sample-failure-log.txt)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@heliohealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe throughput degradation impacting Q4 batch jobs

Alex — thank you for flagging and very sorry for the disruption. We’re treating this as top priority.

Current status: our SRE team traced the spike to a routing change combined with a KV-cache invalidation that created excessive per-request overhead under the large-batch pattern you run. We have an incident timeline and initial mitigation in progress. I’ve included a preliminary timeline as an attachment.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm the total committed monthly spend for Nov and Dec under your reserved plan so we can calculate an appropriate commercial response?
- Can we schedule a 30-min exec-to-exec call today? Grace (Head of Customer Success) and Ben (Account Exec) are looped.

We will come to the call with a proposed settlement that acknowledges the outage and offers a concrete make-good path.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: incident-timeline.csv)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@heliohealth.com>, Eve Stanton <eve.stanton@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliohealth.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed SLA settlement and near-term operational fixes

Alex / Eve / Procurement team — thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, please find the summary and our proposed settlement below. We want to move quickly and keep this operationally focused so HelioHealth can recover confidence by your year-end deadline.

Summary of impact (our analysis):
- Primary impact window: 2026-11-30 20:05–22:40 PST
- Observed error rate peak: 18% (avg: 9% during window)
- Median latency: rose to 1.2s from baseline 120ms
- Root cause: routing misconfiguration + cache invalidation under high-concurrency batch traffic

Operational fixes (already in deploy):
1) Reverted the routing patch and rolled a stability patch (deployed 2026-12-01 02:30 PST).
2) KV-cache guardrails added to prevent full-cache invalidations during high-throughput batches.
3) Dedicated canary pool for HelioHealth’s reserved workloads to isolate future batch patterns.

Proposed settlement (commercial):
- One-time credit equal to 12% of HelioHealth’s committed monthly spend for November 2026 (to acknowledge service impact).
- 25% month discount applied to December 2026 invoice for the reserved capacity associated with batch jobs if you accept the operational mitigations.
- Technical commitment: a scheduled optimization work item (no-cost) to tune batching profiles and KV usage with your engineering team in January.

Attachments: proposed-settlement.pdf (formal credit worksheet). We’ve also attached the incident timeline CSV and a recording of the ops debrief.

Ask: Please review and respond by EOD 2026-12-06 so we can finalize the paperwork (DocuSign link below) or iterate if you need a different structure.

DocuSign (draft): https://docusign.redwood.com/HL-2026-Q4-07
Redwood Jira (incident): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRV-1429

Thanks — Rafael
From: Eve Stanton <eve.stanton@heliohealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@heliohealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA settlement and near-term operational fixes

Rafael — thanks for the detailed write-up and for moving quickly on the mitigation. A few questions from our side:

1) The credit math: can you show the calculation for the 12% credit and the breakdown by workload (batch vs. real-time)? We need line-item visibility for procurement.
2) We appreciate the December discount but would prefer a staggered discount across Q1 if the December pipeline is already committed to partners. Would Redwood consider a 10% credit in Dec + 10% in Jan?
3) We need a written SLA amendment that codifies dedicated canary pools and the KV-cache guardrails.

We’re open to the TC (technical collaboration) item in Jan. Please loop legal if the DocuSign draft is going to change materially.

— Eve
VP Product Operations
HelioHealth
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Eve Stanton <eve.stanton@heliohealth.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@heliohealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA settlement and near-term operational fixes — follow-up

Eve — great questions. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Credit math: we calculated 12% of your committed November reserved spend (line items attached in proposed-settlement.pdf). We’ll produce a line-item breakout (batch vs realtime) for procurement to review; that will be delivered by COB tomorrow.
2) Staggered discount: Redwood is agreeable to split the commercial concession: 8% credit applied to December invoice + 8% applied to January invoice, with an additional 2% one-time credit published now (totaling the same nominal 18% of one month we initially offered across the period). If that structure works for you we’ll amend the DocuSign draft.
3) SLA amendment: Legal and Product have a draft amendment that codifies the dedicated canary pool and KV guardrails. I’ll put Marissa (Legal) on a short thread to pick up changes.

Proposed timeline:
- 2026-12-03: deliver detailed credit line-item breakout to Procurement.
- 2026-12-04: finalize DocuSign draft and SLA amendment.
- 2026-12-06: target sign-off or final counter proposal.

We’re also offering a 60-minute technical working session (Dec 9) to scope the January optimization work.

If acceptable, please reply with a short acceptance (
